previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening right leg cellulitis and acute-on-chronic volume overload following a fall at home. She presented with increased leg redness, warmth, and swelling, along with a 14-pound weight gain. Laboratory results showed leukocytosis, and a chest X-ray ruled out pulmonary congestion. She was treated with IV furosemide for diastolic heart failure, achieving significant diuresis and weight reduction to 348 pounds. Vancomycin was initiated for cellulitis but switched to clindamycin due to skin sloughing and oral ulcerations. Home IV antibiotics, increased oral diuretic therapy with bumetanide, and continued management of chronic conditions including anticoagulation, seizure disorder, and hypothyroidism were arranged. She improved clinically, with reduced infection signs and better mobility, and was discharged home with home health services for wound care, medication administration, and monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with a PMH ofchronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis 
presenting with increasing ___ edema ___ secondary lymphedema,

# ___ edema: This is most likely a worsening of her chronic 
secondary lymphedema caused by her morbid obesity with potential 
contribution by previous surgeries. Initial DDx included 
lymphedema, CHF, chronic venous insufficiency. CHF is unlikely 
given the fact that her BNP is low (with the caveat of reduced 
diagnostic accuracy in the setting of obesity), she denied PND 
or orthopnea, and she does not have evidence of pulmonary edema 
on CXR to suggest worsened dCHF. However, she likely has a 
diastolic component of heart failure as she is diuretic 
responsive. Patient has been successfully diuresed in prior 
admissions with IV lasix 100 BID, this was initially started. 
However, her creatinine worsened likely due to aggressive volume 
removal, so her lasix was dosed daily per her renal function. 
Her weight did not significantly improve but her swelling 
improved over the hospital course. She was continued on home 
spironolactone 50 mg daily. She wrapped and elevated her legs on 
many days. A foley catheter was placed for urine output 
monitoring. 
 
# Confusion with hx of  Seizure disorder: On ___, she was 
found unresponsive, and awoken, she had difficulty speaking with 
some arm twitching. This resolved over the course of a couple 
minutes and afterwards she was transiently confused, some mild 
difficulty coming up with the right words. Neurology consult 
placed ___ for evaluation for possible seizure. She had a 
similar presentation in ___, thought to be due to low Keppra 
level as it is sensitive to volume changes, so can be affected 
with volume overload.  The patient's exam was at baseline. The 
neurology team did not think that the events described were 
concerning for seizure. The patient's prior seizures have been 
significant generalized events. She was recently started on a 
new sedating medications (gabapentin) which may have resulted in 
the event from ___. Her prior events (at least for the past 2 
decades) have all been in the setting of fluid overload or acute 
illness so it was reasonable to keep this on the Ddx (these were 
tonic clonic events). A send out Keppra level was drawn, pending 
on discharge. Home Levetiracetam 1000 mg PO BID and Topiramate 
100 mg PO/NG Q8H were continued without any dose changes.

#Possible Recurrent cellulitis: Patient's had some right foot 
pain and relative erythema which appeared to be more c/w 
lymphedema flare rather than acute cellulitis. However, patient 
had a history of sub clinical cellulitis and thus was 
empirically treated for a 6 day course of IV clindamycin, which 
was discontinued given no change in clinical status. She was 
largely therapeutic on anticoagulation with no calf tenderness 
making DVT less likely. She was continued on home doxycycline 
100mg bid.  

#Neuropathic pain: patient reported shooting pain on right leg, 
likely contribution of fibromyalgia and poor vascular and 
possible neuropathic etiology from chronic lymphedema. Patient 
on chronic narcotics which was not escalated and low dose 
gabapentin 200 TID was started and appeared to help. She may 
have been increasingly sedated though, and may benefit from pain 
medication changes as an outpatient.

#OSA: patient appeared sleepy in the mornings, with morbid 
obesity and history of OSA, not on CPAP at home thus CPAP was 
not started on current admission. 
 
#History of CHF: There does not appear to be evidence of CHF at 
this time. She does have a history of OSA with potential for 
pulmonary hypertrophy and thus RHF. Previous echo showed good LH 
function but did not well visualize RH. ___ echo showed good RV 
function.

#Leukocytosis: WBC on admission 14.4, now improved ___. Given 
active smoking history, this is a common cause of mild 
neutrophilia. It has been estimated that the white blood cell 
(WBC) count in smokers is raised by about 25 percent. Patient 
was afebrile throughout stay, no evidence of consolidation/PNA 
on CXR. 

#Recurrent DVT/PE: coumadin with goal INR ___, coumadin dosed 
daily ranging from ___ mg. dose.
  
#Fibromyalgia : Continued home OxycoDONE and Morphine.

# Tobacco Use:Nicotine Patch 21 mg TD DAILY initiated. She was 
not a candidate for varenicline or bupropion given h/o seizures.
